title: Grok Independent FBS Top 25 (Week 9 / post-Week 8 results, Oct 25 2026)
source: User's weekly Grok automation (Sunday 8:00 AM MT)

method.note: This is the first run of the hybrid system (no prior Grok ranking for movement). Predictive Rank (PR) averages current SP+ and FPI ranks. Résumé Rank (RR) uses the specified point system (+5 top-10 win, +3 top-25 win, +2 road/neutral Power win, +1 other FBS win, –4 unranked loss, –2 ranked loss, +3 undefeated, +2 H2H over higher-predictive team), converted to rank. Combined = 0.40×PR + 0.60×RR (lowest score ranks higher). No overrides. Data drawn from latest SP+, FPI, records, and known results.ESPN +1

notes.risersFallers: Undefeated teams (Miami, Utah, UCLA) get résumé credit without being punished purely for schedule so far; computers still elevate Ohio State, Georgia, and Notre Dame. Utah ranks higher here than some human polls because of the perfect record + solid efficiency (SP+/FPI top-10 range) rather than pure brand. BYU benefits from the Notre Dame win but drops relative to pure AP love after the UCF loss and mid-tier predictive ranks. Other Big 12 notes: Texas Tech and Arizona hold mid-table spots on mixed results; the conference’s chaos (losses by BYU/TTU) is reflected without inflating or punishing unearned. Brand-name teams (Alabama, Texas, Oregon) are not inflated beyond their numbers/résumé; efficient  undefeated or near-undefeated sides are not docked. AP (pre-weekend) had Miami/BYU higher relative to computers; Grok is more predictive-weighted on the top and résumé-weighted on perfect records.

notes.nextWeek: Key games include Ohio State at USC, Georgia vs Florida, Miami vs North Carolina, Utah at Cincinnati, BYU vs Arizona State, and other conference tests. Upsets or close calls involving the undefeateds or one-loss powers (especially Big Ten/SEC/Big 12) could reshuffle the top 10–15 significantly given the hybrid’s balance of efficiency and résumé points. Chaos has been the norm this season.
notes.cfpOutlook:
Projected current top 12 (hybrid-informed, with conference champ auto-bids in mind): 1 Miami (ACC), 2 Ohio State (Big Ten), 3 Georgia (SEC), 4 Notre Dame, 5 Indiana, 6 Utah (Big 12), 7 UCLA, 8 LSU, 9 Texas, 10 Alabama, 11 BYU, 12 Texas Tech / Kentucky / Boise State (G5). Top 4 receive byes.

Big Ten: Ohio State or Indiana most likely champ; UCLA is a real threat as undefeated. Multiple bids possible if they separate.
SEC: Georgia favored; Alabama, LSU, Kentucky, Tennessee, Texas all live. Chaos continues.
Big 12: Utah currently best positioned as undefeated; BYU and Texas Tech still factors despite losses.
ACC: Miami clear favorite.
Independents/G5: Notre Dame is a top-12 lock if it stays in range. Highest G5 (Boise State or similar) gets the auto-bid.
